STATUS AND SCOPE. This is an unverified proof draft for complex dimension three. The exact Bedford–Taylor foundational premise BT below has not been checked in its primary source. No assertion of publication priority is made. The endpoint equivalence is used as supplied in the question.

STATEMENT. Suppose X is a connected compact complex threefold admitting a smooth Hermitian form g with dd^c(g^2)=0 and S=-dd^c g>=0. Positivity here means that the smooth (2,2)-form S wedges every positive (1,1)-form to a nonnegative volume form. Arbitrary zeros of S are allowed. Write V=integral_X g^3. Then, conditional on BT, every bounded genuine g-psh potential u satisfies

integral_X(g+dd^c u)^3 = V+3 integral_X E_u wedge S >= V,

where E_u=(1/2)dd^c(u^2)-u dd^c u is a positive (1,1)-current. Consequently v_minus(g)=V. For every smooth Hermitian h>=c g, c>0, and every smooth positive probability volume dV,

sup_{T in G_h} ||k_T||_{L^(3/2)(dV)} <= c^(-1)V^(-1/3).

The task-supplied endpoint equivalence consequently gives integral_X(h+dd^c u)^3>=c^3 V for EVERY bounded genuine h-psh potential u. Compactness supplies such a positive comparison constant c for any Hermitian h on X. These estimates impose no common bound on the oscillations of the admissible potentials.

NORMALIZATION. Use d^c=(i/(4 pi))(barpartial-partial), hence dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. For smooth real u, du wedge d^c u=(i/(2 pi))partial u wedge barpartial u>=0.

EXACT FOUNDATIONAL PREMISE BT. For locally bounded canonical psh functions, the recursive Bedford–Taylor products are closed order-zero currents, are multilinear under addition of smooth local potentials, and have decreasing continuity under locally uniformly bounded psh approximation. The concrete instances used are (dd^c p_j)^r -> (dd^c p)^r for 1<=r<=3, and p_j dd^c p_j -> p dd^c p when smooth bounded psh p_j decrease to bounded p. The recursion is dd^c[p(dd^c p)^r]=(dd^c p)^(r+1), with smooth closed factors allowed. No global smooth decreasing approximation of an arbitrary Hermitian-psh function is asserted.

The primary-source target is E. Bedford and B. A. Taylor, “A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions,” Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), 1–40, DOI 10.1007/BF02392348. Public searches located bibliographic citations, but the original paper and the exact locations of these instances were NOT inspected. This explicit source-audit requirement remains unfinished.

BOUNDED-POTENTIAL PROOF, CONDITIONAL ON BT.

On a coordinate ball write u=p-a, with p bounded canonical psh and a smooth real. Such a representation follows from the stipulated genuine psh-plus-smooth representative. Define C_r=(dd^c u)^r by expanding dd^c p-dd^c a with BT products. These are globally defined signed closed order-zero currents. Multiplication by the bounded canonical u is legitimate, and

dd^c(u C_r)=C_(r+1), r=0,1,2.

To check this algebraically, put A=dd^c a and expand u C_r=(p-a) sum_l binom(r,l)(dd^c p)^l wedge (-A)^(r-l). All factors except p-a are closed. Applying dd^c to multiplication by p inserts dd^c p; applying it to multiplication by -a inserts -A. Pascal’s identity gives (dd^c p-A)^(r+1). Local multilinearity ensures independence of the smooth decomposition.

Next choose smooth bounded psh p_j decreasing locally to p by convolution on a smaller ball, and set u_j=p_j-a. The chain rule gives

(1/2)dd^c(u_j^2)-u_j dd^c u_j=du_j wedge d^c u_j>=0.

Local uniform boundedness gives u_j^2 -> u^2 in L^1. The weighted instance of BT gives u_j dd^c u_j -> u dd^c u: expand this expression into p_j dd^c p_j-a dd^c p_j-p_j A+a A. The other terms converge by distributional convergence or bounded dominated convergence. Therefore the positive smooth forms converge to E_u. Positivity is preserved under weak convergence. The displayed intrinsic definition shows that the local energy currents glue. This argument does not assume continuity of u or a global smooth approximation.

Expand the stipulated bounded-potential Monge–Ampère measure:

(g+dd^c u)^3=g^3+3g^2 wedge C_1+3g wedge C_2+C_3.

The recursion and distributional Stokes on compact X give

integral C_3=integral dd^c(u C_2)=0,
integral g^2 wedge C_1=integral u dd^c(g^2)=0,
integral g wedge C_2=integral u C_1 wedge dd^c g.

Because dd^c g is d- and d^c-closed, integral dd^c(u^2) wedge dd^c g=0. The definition of E_u therefore gives

integral u C_1 wedge dd^c g=-integral E_u wedge dd^c g=integral E_u wedge S.

This proves the exact mass formula and its inequality. The constant potential u=0 has mass V, so v_minus(g)=V.

FULL-CURRENT COMPARISON, INCLUDING SINGULAR AND DEGENERATE TESTS.

For fixed dV, Gamma_0(T) is independent of the auxiliary Hermitian background used in its matrix representation. Here is the measure-level calculation. In an h-unitary frame let G be the h-relative positive matrix of g, and P the h-density matrix of T. Put a=(1/3)tr(GP)>0. Then sigma_g=g wedge T=a sigma_h. In a g-unitary frame the density matrix is

P_g=a^(-1)G^(1/2)P G^(1/2), with tr(P_g)=3.

Indeed, if a form has h-relative matrix B, its g-relative matrix is G^(-1/2)B G^(-1/2); substituting these matrices in the trace pairing recovers beta wedge T. Moreover det(P_g)=a^(-3)det(G)det(P), and g^3=det(G)h^3. Substitution in Gamma_0 cancels both a and det(G).

This calculation holds sigma_h-almost everywhere with the matrix density of the current. It requires neither a smooth density nor det(P)>0 and does not discard a singular part. Positivity of G and tr(P)=3 bound a away from zero. Constant homogeneity also holds: Gamma_0(bT)=b Gamma_0(T), hence k_(bT)=b k_T.

Now take ANY T in G_h. Let m=integral g wedge T. The inequality h>=c g gives 0<m<=1/c. Thus U=T/m lies in G_g and remains positive and dd^c-closed. The supplied endpoint equivalence, together with v_minus(g)=V, gives ||k_U||_(3/2)<=V^(-1/3). Therefore

||k_T||_(3/2)=m||k_U||_(3/2)<=c^(-1)V^(-1/3).

Applying the same supplied equivalence gives the lower mass c^3 V for every bounded h-psh potential. No maximizer or chosen smooth test family enters this proof.

WHY THE NONZERO CASE IS OUTSIDE THE OLD IDENTITY MECHANISM. If S is nonzero and a strictly positive Hermitian b satisfies dd^c b=0, Stokes gives

0=integral g wedge dd^c b=integral b wedge dd^c g=-integral b wedge S<0,

a contradiction. A nonzero smooth positive (2,2)-form pairs strictly positively with a Hermitian form on an open set. Hence X has no pluriclosed metric, and in particular no metric satisfying both old identities.

LIMITATIONS. The proof is scoped to n=3; the cubic expansion is essential. It does not show that every threefold has such a metric or that an arbitrary plurinegative metric in higher dimension suffices. The criterion lies beyond the excluded identity mechanism, but literature originality has not been established. Primary-source verification of BT remains indispensable and unfinished.

notes.text:
STATUS AND SUPPORT. This unverified note uses n1’s analytic criterion and full-current comparison, conditional on its explicitly stated Bedford–Taylor premise. The geometry, volume calculations and obstruction arguments are reconstructed below. No pre-existing Hopf mass computation, Vaisman theorem or bundle-existence theorem is imported. These examples go beyond the cases excluded in the question; publication priority is not claimed.

GEOMETRIC HYPOTHESES. Let B be a connected compact Kähler surface with Kähler form omega, and pi:X->B a holomorphic principal elliptic bundle with fixed fiber E=C/Lambda. Assume an E-invariant smooth complex (1,0)-form eta is nonzero on every vertical complex tangent, restricts to the invariant form dz on each fiber, and satisfies

d eta=pi^*F, F=alpha+i beta,

with alpha,beta smooth real closed (1,1)-forms on B. Impose the pointwise curvature condition

Q=alpha^2+beta^2>=0, and Q is not identically zero.

This is a geometric sign condition on the base, not a condition on admissible potentials or normalized tests. Q may vanish; one curvature may be indefinite if the other’s positive square compensates. For any constant s>0 put e=i eta wedge bar eta and g=pi^*omega+s e. This is strictly positive: omega is positive on the quotient tangent space and e on its vertical kernel.

CURVATURE AND VOLUME CALCULATIONS. Suppress pullbacks. The type and closedness assumptions give partial eta=0, barpartial eta=F, partial bar eta=bar F, and barpartial bar eta=0. Therefore

partial e=-i eta wedge bar F,
barpartial e=i F wedge bar eta,
partial barpartial e=i F wedge bar F,
dd^c e=-(1/(2*pi))F wedge bar F=-(1/(2*pi))Q.

The final equality follows because degree-two forms commute. Since omega is closed and e^2=0,

g^2=omega^2+2s omega wedge e,
dd^c(g^2)=-(s/pi)omega wedge Q=0.

The last expression is pulled back from degree six on a real four-dimensional base. Thus S=-dd^c g=(s/(2*pi))pi^*Q is positive and nonzero. The n1 hypotheses hold, and n1’s Stokes obstruction proves that X has no pluriclosed metric whatsoever.

Let A_E=integral_E i dz wedge dbar z. Fiber integration gives

V=integral_X g^3=3s A_E integral_B omega^2.

Consequently every bounded genuine g-psh u satisfies

integral_X(g+dd^c u)^3=V+(3s/(2*pi))integral_X E_u wedge pi^*Q>=V.

For every Hermitian h>=c g, every bounded genuine h-psh potential has mass >=c^3 V, and EVERY T in G_h satisfies ||k_T||_(3/2)<=c^(-1)V^(-1/3). Singular and degenerate currents are included through n1’s measure-level comparison.

INDEPENDENT BOUNDED FIBER CHECK. Because pi^*Q is horizontal top degree, distributional differentiation in product charts and Fubini give

integral_X u dd^c u wedge pi^*Q = integral_B Q(b) integral_(E_b) u_b dd^c u_b.

Each u_b is a bounded canonical quasi-subharmonic function: bounded local psh representatives restrict legitimately to every fiber. The signed measure dd^c u_b has uniformly bounded variation, since dd^c u_b+s e|_(E_b) is positive with total mass s A_E.

On the flat torus let H_t be the periodic Gaussian heat kernel, with Laplacian convention Delta exp(i k.x)=-lambda_k exp(i k.x). Fourier expansion and distributional integration give

integral_(E_b)(H_t*u_b)dd^c u_b = -C_E sum_(k!=0) lambda_k exp(-t lambda_k)|u_hat_b(k)|^2<=0,

where C_E>0 converts the chosen flat Laplacian and volume to dd^c. For t>0 the smooth Fourier series is absolutely convergent. The heat approximants are bounded by ||u_b||_infinity and converge to the canonical u_b at every point. For this last assertion, add a local positive quadratic function to make u_b subharmonic: its submean inequality gives the lower limit for radial Gaussian averages, upper semicontinuity gives the upper limit, and Gaussian tails vanish. Dominated convergence against the finite total variation of dd^c u_b then gives integral u_b dd^c u_b<=0. This checks the energy sign for arbitrary bounded restrictions. It does not replace the BT recursion needed for the total mass expansion or its missing primary-source audit.

EXPLICIT FAMILY. Take B=P^1 x P^1, with omega_1,omega_2 the pullbacks of dd^c log(1+|z|^2). Each integrates to 1 on P^1: on the affine chart its form is (i/(2*pi))dz wedge dbar z/(1+|z|^2)^2, whose polar-coordinate integral is 1. For positive integers a,b set

Omega=a omega_1+b omega_2,
L=O(-a,-b),
X=(L minus the zero section)/<v->rho v>, 0<rho<1 real.

Construct L and its norm as tensor products of the tautological lines. In the standard affine chart the squared frame norm is (1+|z_1|^2)^a(1+|z_2|^2)^b. On L minus zero put r=log||v||^2. Then dd^c r=pi^*Omega and eta=partial r satisfies d eta=2*pi*i*pi^*Omega.

Scaling v by a nonzero constant changes r by a constant, so eta descends and is invariant under the elliptic fiber group C^*/rho^Z. The scaling action is free and properly discontinuous because r shifts by the nonzero constant 2 log rho. Local quotients are holomorphic products U x(C^*/rho^Z), with holomorphic transition maps. Compactness follows from the unit-circle bundle over compact B and the radial interval [rho,1], with its ends identified. Connectedness follows from connected base and fiber.

Here alpha=0, beta=2*pi*Omega, so Q=4*pi^2*Omega^2 is everywhere positive. Choose omega=Omega and g=pi^*Omega+s i eta wedge bar eta. On a fiber the logarithmic coordinate z=log w has periods log rho and 2*pi*i. Since i dz wedge dbar z=2 dx dy,

A_E=4*pi*log(1/rho),
integral_B Omega^2=2ab,
V=24*pi*s*a*b*log(1/rho).

Thus a=b=s=1 and rho=exp(-1) give v_minus(g)=24*pi. For ANY smooth Hermitian h>=c g on this X, every bounded genuine h-psh u has mass >=24*pi*c^3, and the full-current endpoint constant is at most c^(-1)(24*pi)^(-1/3).

DISTINCTION FROM SCALAR HOPF. These X have a nonzero real degree-two cohomology class, proved directly as follows. The invariant real forms A=eta+bar eta and B_1=i(eta-bar eta) have independent vertical restrictions and satisfy dA=0 and dB_1=-4*pi*pi^*Omega. If pi^*(omega_1-omega_2)=d zeta, average zeta over the compact elliptic group. An invariant one-form decomposes uniquely as

zeta=pi^*xi+(pi^*f)A+(pi^*j)B_1.

Its horizontal differential forces df=dj=0 by evaluation on one vertical and one horizontal vector. Thus f,j are constants and omega_1-omega_2=d xi-4*pi*j*Omega. Integrating over the two factor spheres gives 1=-4*pi*j*a and -1=-4*pi*j*b, impossible for positive a,b. Hence the pullback class is nonzero.

A scalar Hopf threefold is diffeomorphic to S^5 x S^1 by separating radius and unit vector and quotienting logarithmic radius by its period. Its real H^2 vanishes: averaging a closed two-form over the circle reduces it to a closed two-form on S^5 plus dt times a closed one-form on S^5, both exact. The vanishing of those sphere groups follows from a cover by two contractible hemispherical neighborhoods. Therefore the constructed X are not scalar Hopf threefolds.

There is also no balanced Hermitian metric on these explicit X. The form pi^*Omega is exact, semipositive and nonzero, by dB_1=-4*pi*pi^*Omega. If a Hermitian b_0 were balanced, Stokes and d(b_0^2)=0 would give integral pi^*Omega wedge b_0^2=0. Positivity makes that integral strictly positive, a contradiction. This obstruction is independent of the chosen split metric.

EXCLUSION OF PRIMITIVE ELLIPTIC DEGENERATION. In the stated (1,1)-curvature model, d(g^2)=0 holds precisely when omega wedge F=0. Indeed d(g^2)=2s omega wedge de, with de=i(F wedge bar eta-eta wedge bar F); its two vertical types are independent. Thus balancedness of the split metric means alpha and beta are both omega-primitive.

For a real primitive (1,1)-form alpha on a Kähler surface, alpha^2=-(|alpha|_omega^2/2)omega^2. Diagonalize its Hermitian matrix: the eigenvalues are lambda,-lambda, giving square -lambda^2 omega^2 and norm squared 2lambda^2. Apply this independently to beta. A primitive pair therefore has

Q=-(|alpha|_omega^2+|beta|_omega^2)omega^2/2<=0.

Unless both curvatures vanish, Q is negative somewhere and fails the sufficient condition. Under that opposite sign, the mass formula is V minus a nonnegative energy pairing and allows mass loss. Under the new sign it is V plus a nonnegative pairing and cannot lose mass. The flat pair is already within the old identities. Thus the hypothesis explicitly excludes nonzero primitive (1,1)-curvature degeneration. More generally, the all-potential lower bound excludes every lower-mass sequence on these X for every Hermitian background, regardless of the finite oscillation of each individual potential.

LIMITATIONS. This note does not identify an uninspected particular counterexample with this curvature model. Changing-sign Q, connections with (2,0)-curvature components, arbitrary balanced manifolds, and dimensions greater than three remain outside scope. The inherited BT primary-source audit and literature-priority question remain open.

ARTIFACTS AND EVIDENCE. The full text is proof_n2.txt. Run `python check_exterior.py`; output is check_output.json. With formal real Hermitian curvature matrices A,B, the exact output for Q/omega^2 is det(A)+det(B), namely a1*a2-a3^2-a4^2+b1*b2-b3^2-b4^2. The program verifies the curvature, Gauduchon, volume, primitive-sign and balancedness identities. All ten finite symbolic checks passed. It represents 1/(2*pi) by the positive symbol c and s by q. This evidence is algebraic, not verification of a universal analytic theorem.

notes.text:
The following is a proof of A, including the measure-level comparison needed for the endpoint. All exterior powers are ordinary powers. Throughout, dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π) and d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π). Integrals are over the compact manifold, without boundary. The explicitly granted BT82 and BGL bounded-product results and the granted all-current endpoint equivalence are the only non-elementary premises used.

1. Bounded-potential calculus. Write A=dd^c u for a bounded genuine quasi-psh function. On a relatively compact coordinate ball choose a smooth real φ such that v=u+φ is bounded psh on a larger ball. Radial convolution of v, with radii decreasing to zero, gives smooth psh v_j decreasing to the canonical v and locally uniformly bounded. Put u_j=v_j−φ. This approximation is local; no global smooth approximation preserving g-psh is asserted or needed.

For k=1,2,3 the currents A_j^k converge to A^k, by expanding powers of dd^c v_j−dd^c φ and applying the granted BT continuity with smooth factors. For k=1,2 the weighted currents u_j A_j^k converge to u A^k: expand them into smooth-factor multiples of v_j(dd^c v_j)^ell and (dd^c v_j)^ell and apply BT Theorem 2.4 and ordinary BT continuity. The weight is the genuine canonical representative, as required in that theorem. This also describes explicitly the weighted signed products used here. These constructions agree on overlaps by the granted canonical bounded-product calculus. The smooth identity

dd^c(u_j A_j^k)=A_j^(k+1)

therefore passes to distributions, giving dd^c(u A)=A^2 and dd^c(u A^2)=A^3. The unweighted signed products A^k are closed order-zero currents, and the weighted products u A^k are order-zero currents. The expansion of (g+A)^3 is the BGL bounded-background expansion; positivity of that product when g+A≥0 is the granted BGL proposition.

Since u_j^2 tends locally in L^1 to u^2, the distributions

E_j=(1/2)dd^c(u_j^2)−u_j dd^c u_j=du_j∧d^c u_j=(i/(2π))∂u_j∧bar∂u_j

converge to E=(1/2)dd^c(u^2)−u dd^c u. Each E_j is a positive (1,1)-form. Hence E is a positive (1,1)-current and is order zero. For completeness, positivity gives order zero locally: test each positive scalar component on a nonnegative cutoff equal to one on a fixed compact set; its distribution value bounds its action on all smooth functions supported there by their sup norm. Polarization bounds the other coefficients. Thus each coefficient extends to a Radon measure. This argument also supplies local mass bounds for the approximants from their distributional convergence. No differentiability of the original u is assumed.

2. The exact cubic identity. Assume dim_C X=3, dd^c(g^2)=0, and S=−dd^c g≥0. The form S is dd^c-closed. Distributional integration by parts, with even-degree smooth test forms, gives

∫g^2 A=∫u dd^c(g^2)=0,
∫A^3=∫dd^c(u A^2)=0,
∫g A^2=∫g dd^c(u A)=∫u A dd^c g=−∫u A S.

Also ∫dd^c(u^2) S=∫u^2 dd^c S=0. Consequently ∫E S=−∫u A S=∫g A^2. Expanding the bounded product proves, as an equality of total masses,

∫(g+dd^c u)^3=V+3∫E_u S,     V=∫g^3.

The pairing on the right is a finite integral because E_u is order zero and S is smooth. Positivity of E_u and S makes it nonnegative. Every bounded genuine g-psh u therefore has mass at least V, while u=0 has mass V. Thus v_−(g)=V>0. This proof uses neither an upper bounded-potential mass assumption nor a chosen family of smooth solutions.

3. Intrinsic determinant measure. Fix a smooth positive volume dV. In this paragraph the dimension is any n≥2 and T is any positive (n−1,n−1)-current, without a smoothness or strict-positivity assumption. The definition extends to unnormalized T. For a background h let σ_h=h∧T. Choose a positive scalar measure ν dominating the local matrix coefficients of T; one can use σ_h, or σ_h+σ_h' when comparing backgrounds. In an h-unitary frame put

C_h=(1/n)P_h(dσ_h/dν).

It is a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix ν-almost everywhere and satisfies β∧T=tr(B C_h)ν, where B is the h-relative matrix of β. Thus tr C_h=dσ_h/dν. Where this trace is zero the matrix vanishes, and the determinant density is taken to be zero. The determinant measure in the question is exactly

Γ_(h,dV)(T)=n(dV/h^n)^(1/n) det(C_h)^(1/n)ν.             (1)

Changing ν to another dominating measure gives the same measure, since det(fC)^(1/n)=f det(C)^(1/n) for f≥0, with zero-density sets treated as above.

Let h' have positive definite matrix K in the h-unitary frame. An h'-unitary frame has β-matrix B'=K^(−1/2)B K^(−1/2). The defining trace pairing then gives C_h'=K^(1/2) C_h K^(1/2). In particular

det C_h'=det(K) det C_h,     (h')^n=det(K) h^n.

The two factors cancel in (1). This proves Γ_(h',dV)(T)=Γ_(h,dV)(T) as measures, including the singular and rank-deficient parts of T. Unitary changes of frame also preserve this expression. We denote it Γ_0(T) when dV is fixed. For every constant a>0, replacing T by aT replaces C_h by aC_h in a fixed dominating measure, so Γ_0(aT)=aΓ_0(T), again as a measure. No assertion about determinants only on the absolutely continuous component was used to establish either result. For the dd^c-closed currents in the task, the given absolute continuity of Γ_0 identifies its density k_T and makes these measure identities identities of densities.

There is also a precise volume covariance, if the word background includes the reference volume: for dV'=f dV with f smooth and positive, Γ_(dV')(T)=f^(1/n)Γ_(dV)(T) and k_T'=f^(−(n−1)/n)k_T. Therefore its L^(n/(n−1)) norm is independent of the reference volume. The measure itself is independent of h, not of dV without this covariance.

4. The uniform estimate for all currents. The granted equivalence states that the supremum over the entire G_g is v_−(g)^(−1/3); by step 2 this is V^(−1/3). Now let h≥c g, c>0, and take any T∈G_h. Set a=∫g∧T. Positivity and normalization give 0<a≤c^(−1). The strict inequality a>0 follows because a positive current with zero trace against a positive definite metric is zero, whereas ∫h∧T=1. The current U=T/a belongs to G_g. Step 3 proves k_T=a k_U, even if T is singular or degenerate. Hence

||k_T||_(3/2)≤a V^(−1/3)≤c^(−1)V^(−1/3).

Taking the supremum over every T∈G_h and using the granted equivalence again yields v_−(h)≥c^3 V. This is a bound on all tests and all near-maximizing sequences. For g the smooth current g^2/V belongs to G_g; its density is V^(−1)(g^3/dV)^(2/3), whose L^(3/2) norm is V^(−1/3). It confirms the stated sharp constant, but the upper bound on the entire current space came from the bounded-potential proof and the all-current equivalence. Any Hermitian h on this compact X satisfies h≥c g for some c>0, because the smallest relative eigenvalue has a positive minimum.

5. The pluriclosed obstruction and its relevance. If S is nonzero and p is a smooth positive Hermitian form, then ∫p∧S>0. Pointwise a nonzero positive (2,2)-form has positive trace against p, and its trace stays positive on an open set. If dd^c p=0, integration by parts instead gives

∫p S=−∫p dd^c g=−∫g dd^c p=0,

a contradiction. Thus no pluriclosed Hermitian metric exists. In particular these nonzero-S cases cannot have a metric satisfying the earlier criterion dd^c p=dd^c(p^2)=0. STATUS AND SCOPE. This is an unverified proof draft for complex dimension three. The exact Bedford–Taylor foundational premise BT below has not been checked in its primary source. No assertion of publication priority is made. The endpoint equivalence is used as supplied in the question.

STATEMENT. Suppose X is a connected compact complex threefold admitting a smooth Hermitian form g with dd^c(g^2)=0 and S=-dd^c g>=0. Positivity here means that the smooth (2,2)-form S wedges every positive (1,1)-form to a nonnegative volume form. Arbitrary zeros of S are allowed. Write V=integral_X g^3. Then, conditional on BT, every bounded genuine g-psh potential u satisfies

integral_X(g+dd^c u)^3 = V+3 integral_X E_u wedge S >= V,

where E_u=(1/2)dd^c(u^2)-u dd^c u is a positive (1,1)-current. Consequently v_minus(g)=V. For every smooth Hermitian h>=c g, c>0, and every smooth positive probability volume dV,

sup_{T in G_h} ||k_T||_{L^(3/2)(dV)} <= c^(-1)V^(-1/3).

The task-supplied endpoint equivalence consequently gives integral_X(h+dd^c u)^3>=c^3 V for EVERY bounded genuine h-psh potential u. Compactness supplies such a positive comparison constant c for any Hermitian h on X. These estimates impose no common bound on the oscillations of the admissible potentials.

NORMALIZATION. Use d^c=(i/(4 pi))(barpartial-partial), hence dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. For smooth real u, du wedge d^c u=(i/(2 pi))partial u wedge barpartial u>=0.

EXACT FOUNDATIONAL PREMISE BT. For locally bounded canonical psh functions, the recursive Bedford–Taylor products are closed order-zero currents, are multilinear under addition of smooth local potentials, and have decreasing continuity under locally uniformly bounded psh approximation. The concrete instances used are (dd^c p_j)^r -> (dd^c p)^r for 1<=r<=3, and p_j dd^c p_j -> p dd^c p when smooth bounded psh p_j decrease to bounded p. The recursion is dd^c[p(dd^c p)^r]=(dd^c p)^(r+1), with smooth closed factors allowed. No global smooth decreasing approximation of an arbitrary Hermitian-psh function is asserted.

The primary-source target is E. Bedford and B. A. Taylor, “A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions,” Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), 1–40, DOI 10.1007/BF02392348. Public searches located bibliographic citations, but the original paper and the exact locations of these instances were NOT inspected. This explicit source-audit requirement remains unfinished.

BOUNDED-POTENTIAL PROOF, CONDITIONAL ON BT.

On a coordinate ball write u=p-a, with p bounded canonical psh and a smooth real. Such a representation follows from the stipulated genuine psh-plus-smooth representative. Define C_r=(dd^c u)^r by expanding dd^c p-dd^c a with BT products. These are globally defined signed closed order-zero currents. Multiplication by the bounded canonical u is legitimate, and

dd^c(u C_r)=C_(r+1), r=0,1,2.

To check this algebraically, put A=dd^c a and expand u C_r=(p-a) sum_l binom(r,l)(dd^c p)^l wedge (-A)^(r-l). All factors except p-a are closed. Applying dd^c to multiplication by p inserts dd^c p; applying it to multiplication by -a inserts -A. Pascal’s identity gives (dd^c p-A)^(r+1). Local multilinearity ensures independence of the smooth decomposition.

Next choose smooth bounded psh p_j decreasing locally to p by convolution on a smaller ball, and set u_j=p_j-a. The chain rule gives

(1/2)dd^c(u_j^2)-u_j dd^c u_j=du_j wedge d^c u_j>=0.

Local uniform boundedness gives u_j^2 -> u^2 in L^1. The weighted instance of BT gives u_j dd^c u_j -> u dd^c u: expand this expression into p_j dd^c p_j-a dd^c p_j-p_j A+a A. The other terms converge by distributional convergence or bounded dominated convergence. Therefore the positive smooth forms converge to E_u. Positivity is preserved under weak convergence. The displayed intrinsic definition shows that the local energy currents glue. This argument does not assume continuity of u or a global smooth approximation.

Expand the stipulated bounded-potential Monge–Ampère measure:

(g+dd^c u)^3=g^3+3g^2 wedge C_1+3g wedge C_2+C_3.

The recursion and distributional Stokes on compact X give

integral C_3=integral dd^c(u C_2)=0,
integral g^2 wedge C_1=integral u dd^c(g^2)=0,
integral g wedge C_2=integral u C_1 wedge dd^c g.

Because dd^c g is d- and d^c-closed, integral dd^c(u^2) wedge dd^c g=0. The definition of E_u therefore gives

integral u C_1 wedge dd^c g=-integral E_u wedge dd^c g=integral E_u wedge S.

This proves the exact mass formula and its inequality. The constant potential u=0 has mass V, so v_minus(g)=V.

FULL-CURRENT COMPARISON, INCLUDING SINGULAR AND DEGENERATE TESTS.

For fixed dV, Gamma_0(T) is independent of the auxiliary Hermitian background used in its matrix representation. Here is the measure-level calculation. In an h-unitary frame let G be the h-relative positive matrix of g, and P the h-density matrix of T. Put a=(1/3)tr(GP)>0. Then sigma_g=g wedge T=a sigma_h. In a g-unitary frame the density matrix is

P_g=a^(-1)G^(1/2)P G^(1/2), with tr(P_g)=3.

Indeed, if a form has h-relative matrix B, its g-relative matrix is G^(-1/2)B G^(-1/2); substituting these matrices in the trace pairing recovers beta wedge T. Moreover det(P_g)=a^(-3)det(G)det(P), and g^3=det(G)h^3. Substitution in Gamma_0 cancels both a and det(G).

This calculation holds sigma_h-almost everywhere with the matrix density of the current. It requires neither a smooth density nor det(P)>0 and does not discard a singular part. Positivity of G and tr(P)=3 bound a away from zero. Constant homogeneity also holds: Gamma_0(bT)=b Gamma_0(T), hence k_(bT)=b k_T.

Now take ANY T in G_h. Let m=integral g wedge T. The inequality h>=c g gives 0<m<=1/c. Thus U=T/m lies in G_g and remains positive and dd^c-closed. The supplied endpoint equivalence, together with v_minus(g)=V, gives ||k_U||_(3/2)<=V^(-1/3). Therefore

||k_T||_(3/2)=m||k_U||_(3/2)<=c^(-1)V^(-1/3).

Applying the same supplied equivalence gives the lower mass c^3 V for every bounded h-psh potential. No maximizer or chosen smooth test family enters this proof.

WHY THE NONZERO CASE IS OUTSIDE THE OLD IDENTITY MECHANISM. If S is nonzero and a strictly positive Hermitian b satisfies dd^c b=0, Stokes gives

0=integral g wedge dd^c b=integral b wedge dd^c g=-integral b wedge S<0,

a contradiction. A nonzero smooth positive (2,2)-form pairs strictly positively with a Hermitian form on an open set. Hence X has no pluriclosed metric, and in particular no metric satisfying both old identities.

LIMITATIONS. The proof is scoped to n=3; the cubic expansion is essential. It does not show that every threefold has such a metric or that an arbitrary plurinegative metric in higher dimension suffices. The criterion lies beyond the excluded identity mechanism, but literature originality has not been established. Primary-source verification of BT remains indispensable and unfinished.

STATUS AND SUPPORT. This unverified note uses n1’s analytic criterion and full-current comparison, conditional on its explicitly stated Bedford–Taylor premise. The geometry, volume calculations and obstruction arguments are reconstructed below. No pre-existing Hopf mass computation, Vaisman theorem or bundle-existence theorem is imported. These examples go beyond the cases excluded in the question; publication priority is not claimed.

GEOMETRIC HYPOTHESES. Let B be a connected compact Kähler surface with Kähler form omega, and pi:X->B a holomorphic principal elliptic bundle with fixed fiber E=C/Lambda. Assume an E-invariant smooth complex (1,0)-form eta is nonzero on every vertical complex tangent, restricts to the invariant form dz on each fiber, and satisfies

d eta=pi^*F, F=alpha+i beta,

with alpha,beta smooth real closed (1,1)-forms on B. Impose the pointwise curvature condition

Q=alpha^2+beta^2>=0, and Q is not identically zero.

This is a geometric sign condition on the base, not a condition on admissible potentials or normalized tests. Q may vanish; one curvature may be indefinite if the other’s positive square compensates. For any constant s>0 put e=i eta wedge bar eta and g=pi^*omega+s e. This is strictly positive: omega is positive on the quotient tangent space and e on its vertical kernel.

CURVATURE AND VOLUME CALCULATIONS. Suppress pullbacks. The type and closedness assumptions give partial eta=0, barpartial eta=F, partial bar eta=bar F, and barpartial bar eta=0. Therefore

partial e=-i eta wedge bar F,
barpartial e=i F wedge bar eta,
partial barpartial e=i F wedge bar F,
dd^c e=-(1/(2*pi))F wedge bar F=-(1/(2*pi))Q.

The final equality follows because degree-two forms commute. Since omega is closed and e^2=0,

g^2=omega^2+2s omega wedge e,
dd^c(g^2)=-(s/pi)omega wedge Q=0.

The last expression is pulled back from degree six on a real four-dimensional base. Thus S=-dd^c g=(s/(2*pi))pi^*Q is positive and nonzero. The n1 hypotheses hold, and n1’s Stokes obstruction proves that X has no pluriclosed metric whatsoever.

Let A_E=integral_E i dz wedge dbar z. Fiber integration gives

V=integral_X g^3=3s A_E integral_B omega^2.

Consequently every bounded genuine g-psh u satisfies

integral_X(g+dd^c u)^3=V+(3s/(2*pi))integral_X E_u wedge pi^*Q>=V.

For every Hermitian h>=c g, every bounded genuine h-psh potential has mass >=c^3 V, and EVERY T in G_h satisfies ||k_T||_(3/2)<=c^(-1)V^(-1/3). Singular and degenerate currents are included through n1’s measure-level comparison.

INDEPENDENT BOUNDED FIBER CHECK. Because pi^*Q is horizontal top degree, distributional differentiation in product charts and Fubini give

integral_X u dd^c u wedge pi^*Q = integral_B Q(b) integral_(E_b) u_b dd^c u_b.

Each u_b is a bounded canonical quasi-subharmonic function: bounded local psh representatives restrict legitimately to every fiber. The signed measure dd^c u_b has uniformly bounded variation, since dd^c u_b+s e|_(E_b) is positive with total mass s A_E.

On the flat torus let H_t be the periodic Gaussian heat kernel, with Laplacian convention Delta exp(i k.x)=-lambda_k exp(i k.x). Fourier expansion and distributional integration give

integral_(E_b)(H_t*u_b)dd^c u_b = -C_E sum_(k!=0) lambda_k exp(-t lambda_k)|u_hat_b(k)|^2<=0,

where C_E>0 converts the chosen flat Laplacian and volume to dd^c. For t>0 the smooth Fourier series is absolutely convergent. The heat approximants are bounded by ||u_b||_infinity and converge to the canonical u_b at every point. For this last assertion, add a local positive quadratic function to make u_b subharmonic: its submean inequality gives the lower limit for radial Gaussian averages, upper semicontinuity gives the upper limit, and Gaussian tails vanish. Dominated convergence against the finite total variation of dd^c u_b then gives integral u_b dd^c u_b<=0. This checks the energy sign for arbitrary bounded restrictions. It does not replace the BT recursion needed for the total mass expansion or its missing primary-source audit.

EXPLICIT FAMILY. Take B=P^1 x P^1, with omega_1,omega_2 the pullbacks of dd^c log(1+|z|^2). Each integrates to 1 on P^1: on the affine chart its form is (i/(2*pi))dz wedge dbar z/(1+|z|^2)^2, whose polar-coordinate integral is 1. For positive integers a,b set

Omega=a omega_1+b omega_2,
L=O(-a,-b),
X=(L minus the zero section)/<v->rho v>, 0<rho<1 real.

Construct L and its norm as tensor products of the tautological lines. In the standard affine chart the squared frame norm is (1+|z_1|^2)^a(1+|z_2|^2)^b. On L minus zero put r=log||v||^2. Then dd^c r=pi^*Omega and eta=partial r satisfies d eta=2*pi*i*pi^*Omega.

Scaling v by a nonzero constant changes r by a constant, so eta descends and is invariant under the elliptic fiber group C^*/rho^Z. The scaling action is free and properly discontinuous because r shifts by the nonzero constant 2 log rho. Local quotients are holomorphic products U x(C^*/rho^Z), with holomorphic transition maps. Compactness follows from the unit-circle bundle over compact B and the radial interval [rho,1], with its ends identified. Connectedness follows from connected base and fiber.

Here alpha=0, beta=2*pi*Omega, so Q=4*pi^2*Omega^2 is everywhere positive. Choose omega=Omega and g=pi^*Omega+s i eta wedge bar eta. On a fiber the logarithmic coordinate z=log w has periods log rho and 2*pi*i. Since i dz wedge dbar z=2 dx dy,

A_E=4*pi*log(1/rho),
integral_B Omega^2=2ab,
V=24*pi*s*a*b*log(1/rho).

Thus a=b=s=1 and rho=exp(-1) give v_minus(g)=24*pi. For ANY smooth Hermitian h>=c g on this X, every bounded genuine h-psh u has mass >=24*pi*c^3, and the full-current endpoint constant is at most c^(-1)(24*pi)^(-1/3).

DISTINCTION FROM SCALAR HOPF. These X have a nonzero real degree-two cohomology class, proved directly as follows. The invariant real forms A=eta+bar eta and B_1=i(eta-bar eta) have independent vertical restrictions and satisfy dA=0 and dB_1=-4*pi*pi^*Omega. If pi^*(omega_1-omega_2)=d zeta, average zeta over the compact elliptic group. An invariant one-form decomposes uniquely as

zeta=pi^*xi+(pi^*f)A+(pi^*j)B_1.

Its horizontal differential forces df=dj=0 by evaluation on one vertical and one horizontal vector. Thus f,j are constants and omega_1-omega_2=d xi-4*pi*j*Omega. Integrating over the two factor spheres gives 1=-4*pi*j*a and -1=-4*pi*j*b, impossible for positive a,b. Hence the pullback class is nonzero.

A scalar Hopf threefold is diffeomorphic to S^5 x S^1 by separating radius and unit vector and quotienting logarithmic radius by its period. Its real H^2 vanishes: averaging a closed two-form over the circle reduces it to a closed two-form on S^5 plus dt times a closed one-form on S^5, both exact. The vanishing of those sphere groups follows from a cover by two contractible hemispherical neighborhoods. Therefore the constructed X are not scalar Hopf threefolds.

There is also no balanced Hermitian metric on these explicit X. The form pi^*Omega is exact, semipositive and nonzero, by dB_1=-4*pi*pi^*Omega. If a Hermitian b_0 were balanced, Stokes and d(b_0^2)=0 would give integral pi^*Omega wedge b_0^2=0. Positivity makes that integral strictly positive, a contradiction. This obstruction is independent of the chosen split metric.

EXCLUSION OF PRIMITIVE ELLIPTIC DEGENERATION. In the stated (1,1)-curvature model, d(g^2)=0 holds precisely when omega wedge F=0. Indeed d(g^2)=2s omega wedge de, with de=i(F wedge bar eta-eta wedge bar F); its two vertical types are independent. Thus balancedness of the split metric means alpha and beta are both omega-primitive.

For a real primitive (1,1)-form alpha on a Kähler surface, alpha^2=-(|alpha|_omega^2/2)omega^2. Diagonalize its Hermitian matrix: the eigenvalues are lambda,-lambda, giving square -lambda^2 omega^2 and norm squared 2lambda^2. Apply this independently to beta. A primitive pair therefore has

Q=-(|alpha|_omega^2+|beta|_omega^2)omega^2/2<=0.

Unless both curvatures vanish, Q is negative somewhere and fails the sufficient condition. Under that opposite sign, the mass formula is V minus a nonnegative energy pairing and allows mass loss. Under the new sign it is V plus a nonnegative pairing and cannot lose mass. The flat pair is already within the old identities. Thus the hypothesis explicitly excludes nonzero primitive (1,1)-curvature degeneration. More generally, the all-potential lower bound excludes every lower-mass sequence on these X for every Hermitian background, regardless of the finite oscillation of each individual potential.

LIMITATIONS. This note does not identify an uninspected particular counterexample with this curvature model. Changing-sign Q, connections with (2,0)-curvature components, arbitrary balanced manifolds, and dimensions greater than three remain outside scope. The inherited BT primary-source audit and literature-priority question remain open.

With formal real Hermitian curvature matrices A,B, the exact output for Q/omega^2 is det(A)+det(B), namely a1*a2-a3^2-a4^2+b1*b2-b3^2-b4^2. The program verifies the curvature, Gauduchon, volume, primitive-sign and balancedness identities. All ten finite symbolic checks passed. It represents 1/(2*pi) by the positive symbol c and s by q. This evidence is algebraic, not verification of a universal analytic theorem.

The following is a proof of A, including the measure-level comparison needed for the endpoint. All exterior powers are ordinary powers. Throughout, dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π) and d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π). Integrals are over the compact manifold, without boundary. The explicitly granted BT82 and BGL bounded-product results and the granted all-current endpoint equivalence are the only non-elementary premises used.

1. Bounded-potential calculus. Write A=dd^c u for a bounded genuine quasi-psh function. On a relatively compact coordinate ball choose a smooth real φ such that v=u+φ is bounded psh on a larger ball. Radial convolution of v, with radii decreasing to zero, gives smooth psh v_j decreasing to the canonical v and locally uniformly bounded. Put u_j=v_j−φ. This approximation is local; no global smooth approximation preserving g-psh is asserted or needed.

For k=1,2,3 the currents A_j^k converge to A^k, by expanding powers of dd^c v_j−dd^c φ and applying the granted BT continuity with smooth factors. For k=1,2 the weighted currents u_j A_j^k converge to u A^k: expand them into smooth-factor multiples of v_j(dd^c v_j)^ell and (dd^c v_j)^ell and apply BT Theorem 2.4 and ordinary BT continuity. The weight is the genuine canonical representative, as required in that theorem. This also describes explicitly the weighted signed products used here. These constructions agree on overlaps by the granted canonical bounded-product calculus. The smooth identity

dd^c(u_j A_j^k)=A_j^(k+1)

therefore passes to distributions, giving dd^c(u A)=A^2 and dd^c(u A^2)=A^3. The unweighted signed products A^k are closed order-zero currents, and the weighted products u A^k are order-zero currents. The expansion of (g+A)^3 is the BGL bounded-background expansion; positivity of that product when g+A≥0 is the granted BGL proposition.

Since u_j^2 tends locally in L^1 to u^2, the distributions

E_j=(1/2)dd^c(u_j^2)−u_j dd^c u_j=du_j∧d^c u_j=(i/(2π))∂u_j∧bar∂u_j

converge to E=(1/2)dd^c(u^2)−u dd^c u. Each E_j is a positive (1,1)-form. Hence E is a positive (1,1)-current and is order zero. For completeness, positivity gives order zero locally: test each positive scalar component on a nonnegative cutoff equal to one on a fixed compact set; its distribution value bounds its action on all smooth functions supported there by their sup norm. Polarization bounds the other coefficients. Thus each coefficient extends to a Radon measure. This argument also supplies local mass bounds for the approximants from their distributional convergence. No differentiability of the original u is assumed.

2. The exact cubic identity. Assume dim_C X=3, dd^c(g^2)=0, and S=−dd^c g≥0. The form S is dd^c-closed. Distributional integration by parts, with even-degree smooth test forms, gives

∫g^2 A=∫u dd^c(g^2)=0,
∫A^3=∫dd^c(u A^2)=0,
∫g A^2=∫g dd^c(u A)=∫u A dd^c g=−∫u A S.

Also ∫dd^c(u^2) S=∫u^2 dd^c S=0. Consequently ∫E S=−∫u A S=∫g A^2. Expanding the bounded product proves, as an equality of total masses,

∫(g+dd^c u)^3=V+3∫E_u S,     V=∫g^3.

The pairing on the right is a finite integral because E_u is order zero and S is smooth. Positivity of E_u and S makes it nonnegative. Every bounded genuine g-psh u therefore has mass at least V, while u=0 has mass V. Thus v_−(g)=V>0. This proof uses neither an upper bounded-potential mass assumption nor a chosen family of smooth solutions.

3. Intrinsic determinant measure. Fix a smooth positive volume dV. In this paragraph the dimension is any n≥2 and T is any positive (n−1,n−1)-current, without a smoothness or strict-positivity assumption. The definition extends to unnormalized T. For a background h let σ_h=h∧T. Choose a positive scalar measure ν dominating the local matrix coefficients of T; one can use σ_h, or σ_h+σ_h' when comparing backgrounds. In an h-unitary frame put

C_h=(1/n)P_h(dσ_h/dν).

It is a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix ν-almost everywhere and satisfies β∧T=tr(B C_h)ν, where B is the h-relative matrix of β. Thus tr C_h=dσ_h/dν. Where this trace is zero the matrix vanishes, and the determinant density is taken to be zero. The determinant measure in the question is exactly

Γ_(h,dV)(T)=n(dV/h^n)^(1/n) det(C_h)^(1/n)ν.             (1)

Changing ν to another dominating measure gives the same measure, since det(fC)^(1/n)=f det(C)^(1/n) for f≥0, with zero-density sets treated as above.

Let h' have positive definite matrix K in the h-unitary frame. An h'-unitary frame has β-matrix B'=K^(−1/2)B K^(−1/2). The defining trace pairing then gives C_h'=K^(1/2) C_h K^(1/2). In particular

det C_h'=det(K) det C_h,     (h')^n=det(K) h^n.

The two factors cancel in (1). This proves Γ_(h',dV)(T)=Γ_(h,dV)(T) as measures, including the singular and rank-deficient parts of T. Unitary changes of frame also preserve this expression. We denote it Γ_0(T) when dV is fixed. For every constant a>0, replacing T by aT replaces C_h by aC_h in a fixed dominating measure, so Γ_0(aT)=aΓ_0(T), again as a measure. No assertion about determinants only on the absolutely continuous component was used to establish either result. For the dd^c-closed currents in the task, the given absolute continuity of Γ_0 identifies its density k_T and makes these measure identities identities of densities.

There is also a precise volume covariance, if the word background includes the reference volume: for dV'=f dV with f smooth and positive, Γ_(dV')(T)=f^(1/n)Γ_(dV)(T) and k_T'=f^(−(n−1)/n)k_T. Therefore its L^(n/(n−1)) norm is independent of the reference volume. The measure itself is independent of h, not of dV without this covariance.

4. The uniform estimate for all currents. The granted equivalence states that the supremum over the entire G_g is v_−(g)^(−1/3); by step 2 this is V^(−1/3). Now let h≥c g, c>0, and take any T∈G_h. The current U=T/a belongs to G_g. Step 3 proves k_T=a k_U, even if T is singular or degenerate. Hence

||k_T||_(3/2)≤a V^(−1/3)≤c^(−1)V^(−1/3).

Taking the supremum over every T∈G_h and using the granted equivalence again yields v_−(h)≥c^3 V. This is a bound on all tests and all near-maximizing sequences. For g the smooth current g^2/V belongs to G_g; its density is V^(−1)(g^3/dV)^(2/3), whose L^(3/2) norm is V^(−1/3). It confirms the stated sharp constant, but the upper bound on the entire current space came from the bounded-potential proof and the all-current equivalence. Any Hermitian h on this compact X satisfies h≥c g for some c>0, because the smallest relative eigenvalue has a positive minimum.

5. The pluriclosed obstruction and its relevance. If S is nonzero and p is a smooth positive Hermitian form, then ∫p∧S>0. Pointwise a nonzero positive (2,2)-form has positive trace against p, and its trace stays positive on an open set. If dd^c p=0, integration by parts instead gives

∫p S=−∫p dd^c g=−∫g dd^c p=0,

a contradiction. Thus no pluriclosed Hermitian metric exists. In particular these nonzero-S cases cannot have a metric satisfying the earlier criterion dd^c p=dd^c(p^2)=0. The new condition instead controls the sign of the bounded-potential energy. It directly prevents masses from approaching zero by forcing every such mass to be at least V, and through the given equivalence prevents failure of the full-current endpoint.

This proves B and identifies exactly what the curvature criterion says about primitive elliptic bundles. The bounded-potential and full-current results of n1 are used. No bundle classification or vanishing theorem is used.

Let π:X→B be the specified holomorphic principal elliptic bundle over a compact connected Kähler surface, with invariant (1,0)-form η restricting to dz on the fiber E=C/Λ. Pullbacks of base forms are suppressed temporarily in the calculation. Since dη=F=α+iβ has type (1,1),

∂η=0,   bar∂η=F,   ∂barη=bar F,   bar∂barη=0.

Closedness and pure type of F imply ∂F=bar∂F=0, and likewise for bar F. Put θ=iη∧barη. The graded product rule gives

bar∂θ=iF∧barη,
∂bar∂θ=iF∧bar F,
dd^c θ=−F∧bar F/(2π)=−(α^2+β^2)/(2π).

Here real two-forms commute, so the cross terms cancel. Thus for g=πω+sθ,

dd^c g=−sπQ/(2π),       Q=α^2+β^2.

The form g is positive definite: πω is positive on the quotient of the tangent space by the vertical complex line, and θ is positive on that line because η restricts to dz. If both terms vanish on a vector, that vector is vertical and η on it vanishes, so it is zero. Also θ^2=0, and base dimension two gives

g^2=(πω)^2+2sπω∧θ,
dd^c(g^2)=2sπω∧dd^c θ=−(s/π)π(ω∧Q)=0.

There are no omitted mixed differential terms in this equality, because the pulled-back ω is both ∂- and bar∂-closed. The nonzero volume term is

g^3=3sπ(ω^2)∧iη∧barη.

In local holomorphic bundle charts, terms of η containing horizontal differentials disappear when wedged with the base top form. Fubini's theorem and a partition of unity on B therefore give

V=∫_X g^3=3s A_E ∫_B ω^2,       A_E=∫_E i dz∧dbar z.

The total space is compact and connected: finitely many relatively compact local trivializations over the compact connected base have compact torus fibers, and a path in the base can be lifted piecewise, with any two resulting endpoints joined in the connected fiber. Thus n1 applies with S=(s/(2π))πQ whenever Q≥0. In the stipulated nonzero case S is nonzero. Consequently, for every bounded genuine g-psh u,

∫_X(g+dd^c u)^3=V+(3s/(2π))∫_X E_u∧πQ,
v_−(g)=V.

For every Hermitian h≥c g and every smooth positive probability dV, every T∈G_h satisfies ||k_T||_(3/2)≤c^(−1)V^(−1/3), and v_−(h)≥c^3 V. These statements include singular and degenerate currents. There is no pluriclosed Hermitian metric, by n1.

For clarity the balancedness calculation, including its converse for this particular g, is as follows:

dθ=i(F∧barη−η∧bar F),
d(g^2)=2siπω∧(πF∧barη−η∧πbar F).                 (2)

Because the fiber complex cotangent line has independent (1,0) and (0,1) parts, contracting (2) with a vertical (0,1) vector satisfying barη=1 and then a vertical (1,0) vector satisfying η=1 shows that d(g^2)=0 implies ω∧F=ω∧bar F=0. Conversely these equalities make (2) vanish. They are equivalent to ω∧α=ω∧β=0. Thus this g is balanced if and only if both real curvatures are ω-primitive. This is a formula about this metric; it does not assert that every possible metric on an arbitrary bundle has the same property.

The primitive sign can be established without a Hodge theorem. At a point choose an ω-unitary frame. The Hermitian matrix H of a real primitive (1,1)-form χ has trace zero. Diagonalizing it gives eigenvalues λ,−λ. Its squared norm is |χ|^2=tr(H^2)=2λ^2 in this convention, and χ^2=det(H)ω^2=−λ^2ω^2. Hence

χ^2=−(|χ|^2/2)ω^2,
Q=−(|α|^2+|β|^2)ω^2/2                         (3)

when both curvatures are primitive. In particular nonzero primitive curvature gives Q<0 wherever the pair is nonzero, and cannot satisfy Q≥0 everywhere. The previously proved cubic identity, which algebraically holds also for signed Q, then has the opposite sign:

∫(g+dd^c u)^3=V−(3s/(4π))∫E_u∧π((|α|^2+|β|^2)ω^2)≤V.

One can even make the inequality strict for a smooth small potential, without asserting zero lower mass. Choose a small local bundle chart over an open set where the coefficient in (3) is positive. Taking the ath and bth tensor powers on the two factors constructs L=O(−a,−b) with local frame e whose squared norm is

||e||^2=(1+|z1|^2)^a(1+|z2|^2)^b=e^ψ.

For a nonzero vector v=λe, the globally defined real function on L^times is r=log||v||^2=log|λ|^2+ψ. Since λ never vanishes,

η=∂r=dλ/λ+∂ψ,
dη=bar∂∂r=2πiπΩ.                            (1)

This also checks the sign of the tautological curvature against the exact frame norm required in the target.

Let 0<ρ<1 and ℓ=log(1/ρ)>0. The action v↦ρ^k v, k∈Z, is holomorphic and free. It is properly discontinuous: on any compact subsets of L^times the function r lies in bounded intervals, whereas this action changes r by −2kℓ, so only finitely many k can make the subsets meet. Each point has a sufficiently small complex neighborhood disjoint from all its nonidentity translates; the quotient therefore has holomorphic charts, with holomorphic transition maps, and is a Hausdorff complex manifold X of dimension three.

The map to B is a holomorphic principal elliptic bundle. On a local frame chart it is the product U×(C^times/ρ^Z). The exponential map identifies

C^times/ρ^Z=C/(2πiZ+(logρ)Z)=:E.

The two periods are real-linearly independent, giving a compact complex torus. Frame changes multiply λ by nowhere-zero holomorphic functions, and thus induce holomorphic translations of E (use local logarithms; changing a logarithm adds a period). Scalar multiplication by C^times/ρ^Z supplies a globally defined, free and transitive fiber action. The function r does not itself descend, but its change under ρ is a constant. It does not use a Calabi–Eckmann, LCK, or Vaisman classification. In fact the no-LCK argument works for every parameter in the stated range, which includes τ=−1+i.

Write τ=A+iB with A<0 and B>0. Let M=(C^2 minus {0})×(C^2 minus {0}), and let the additive complex Lie group C act by t·(z,w)=(e^t z,e^(τt)w).

1. Freeness, properness and topology. Freeness can be read off directly: a stabilizer t must satisfy e^t=e^(τt)=1. The first equality gives t=2πik for an integer k, and Re(τt)=−2πBk=0 gives k=0. There is a stronger global description. For r1=log||z||^2, r2=log||w||^2, the action by t=x+iy changes them to

r1+2x,       r2+2(Ax−By).

Every orbit meets S^3×S^3, the locus r1=r2=0, exactly once. The unique element taking a point to this locus has x=−r1/2, y=(r2−Ar1)/(2B). Equivalently

Φ:C×S^3×S^3→M,   Φ(t,u,v)=(e^t u,e^(τt)v)

is a smooth diffeomorphism with inverse

t=r1/2+i(Ar1−r2)/(2B),     u=e^(−t)z,     v=e^(−τt)w.

All formulas are smooth and have norms ||u||=||v||=1. The action in these coordinates is translation on the first C factor. Translation is proper: if a point and its translate range in compact sets, both their C coordinates and their difference remain in compact sets, and the sphere factors are already compact. More formally, the inverse image of a compact set under (a,(t,p))↦((t,p),(a+t,p)) is closed and bounded in the C coordinates and has compact sphere coordinates. Thus the action is proper. Its topological/smooth quotient is Hausdorff, compact, and diffeomorphic to S^3×S^3. This description will also show that any closed real one-form on the quotient is exact.

2. Explicit complex charts and the elliptic principal bundle. Projectivization (z,w)↦([z],[w]) is invariant. In a product affine chart U of P^1×P^1, write

z=λ(1,u),     w=μ(1,v),     λ,μ∈C^times.

On the logarithmic covering of (C^times)^2 put ξ=logλ and χ=logμ. The action is (ξ,χ)↦(ξ+t,χ+τt), whose invariant complex coordinate is ζ=τξ−χ. Changing logarithms adds

2πiτ m−2πi n,        m,n∈Z.

Therefore the target is E=C/Λ with Λ=<2πiτ,−2πi>. The period vectors have real components (−2πB,2πA) and (0,−2π), which are independent because B>0. The map (λ,μ)↦[τlogλ−logμ] is a well-defined holomorphic surjection to E: local logarithms make it holomorphic, and varying μ supplies any ζ. Its fibers are precisely C-orbits. Indeed equal images allow the logarithms to be shifted by integer periods so that the two ζ values agree exactly; then Δχ=τΔξ and the two points differ by the action with t=Δξ.

The map U×(C^times)^2→U×E is a holomorphic submersion: on a logarithmic chart the derivative (τ,−1) in the fiber is nonzero. It is open, as is seen by using the coordinates (u,v,ξ,ζ). Normalizing this representative with the explicit inverse of Φ gives a smooth local map to S^3×S^3. Conversely the invariant coordinates restricted to the smooth normalized slice are smooth. Thus the complex charts have the same underlying smooth structure as the quotient already constructed. On overlaps the scalar frame changes for z,w multiply λ,μ by nonzero holomorphic functions a(u),b(v); the ζ coordinates change by τlog a−log b, interpreted modulo Λ. These are holomorphic translations. This proves directly that these quotient charts define a complex manifold of dimension three and that projectivization is a holomorphic elliptic bundle.

For explicit principality, a complex number c acts on M by (z,w)↦(z,e^(−c)w), commuting with the original C-action and inducing ζ↦ζ+c. A change of c by −2πin acts trivially on M, and a change by 2πiτm differs from the original action with t=−2πim, since that action fixes z and multiplies w by e^(−2πiτm). Thus this action factors through E. In each U×E chart it is translation, so it is free and transitive on every fiber. No assertion about a preclassified quotient was needed.

3. The connection and its curvature. On M, η=τ∂r1−∂r2. For fixed action element t, the functions r1,r2 change by constants, so η is invariant. The holomorphic fundamental vector V=(sum z_j∂_(z_j))+τ(sum w_j∂_(w_j)) satisfies ∂r1(V)=1 and ∂r2(V)=τ. Hence η(V)=0; because η has type (1,0) it also annihilates bar V. r1=log|λ|^2+ψ1,   r2=log|μ|^2+ψ2,

Pointwise positivity instead gives πω1∧p^2>0. Therefore no balanced metric exists. In particular no Kähler metric exists, since the square of a closed Hermitian form is closed. It would be a Kähler metric, contradicting the previous exact-form obstruction. This proves no LCK metric exists for all A<0, B>0, in particular for τ=−1+i.
